correctness.rationale: The exact domain is all indexed binary rings of length n>=3 under the simultaneous local truth table f=1 on 000,011,110. Period-t time-column closed walks are in bijection with Fix(F^t) for t=1,2,3,6. The integer graph determinant identities were rederived and all coefficients reproduced from the packaged verification/verify_transfer.py, then inclusion-exclusion gives 6c_n=T6-T3-T2+T1. Exact traces prove the 8,9,10,11 gap. Twelve actual based graph walks of consecutive lengths 12..23 visit period-two and period-three columns; concatenating at vertex 21 proves primitive six-periodic states at every n>=12 without finite extrapolation. The 23-node SCC has explicit 3- and 4-cycles; exact positive-vector rational Perron enclosures separate its leading root (1.61574,1.61576) from smaller temporal-three/two growth. verification/check_direct.py independently checked every binary initial state at lengths 3..15. All needed scripts and output files are included with this record. Limit: other temporal periods and transient basins are not claimed.

originality.rationale: Exact same-rule published results on periods one, two, and three do not give the sixth-return determinant E, the six-cycle support reentrance or its growth base. Sutner addresses period-three existence, while Stricker reports finite cycle spectra and might already cover several finite examples, but not the all-circumference rational six-cycle count or concatenation theorem. Wolfram describes generic repetition constraints and finite sample dots. Kang studies spaced-neighbor Rule 73 and Rule 109, not the nearest-neighbor map. The comparison distinguishes the classical finite transfer method (not new) from the explicit non-implied formula and exact natural support. Historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Wolfram visual period charts and Stricker finite tables may already enumerate the short 8,9,10,11,12 examples; only the infinite rational census, support proof and entropy are assessed as original.
Some unindexed Rule 73 or Rule 109 transfer-matrix computations may yield equivalent sixth-period formulas; novelty is best knowledge, not an independence or priority certificate.
